assign.request: A persistent, resizable left sidebar, a viewport beside it, and a tree of homepage designs derived one change at a time — /layouts/shell/
assign.now: scoping — read the brief, core/Page, ux/Tree, the practice layouts
steps: Scope: brief, core/Page render+store, ux/Tree, the sticky-rail idiom
Test the three derivation mechanisms against core, pick one
Build the shell: sidebar + viewport, edge to edge
Build the design tree: a base Home and seven derivations
Resize the rail by its right edge, remember the width
Measure: nav stability at 1280/1920/3440, the three invariants in the viewport

log.msg: DERIVATION PROBE, run against the real core Page in a real browser (scratchpad/shell-lab-derive-probe.mjs). (a) subclass per design: declare() runs, fresh children Map, url/name/title right - but core builds a PLAIN Page for every POJO child, so a subclass only ever arrives via a real page.js file. (b) Object.create(parent)+assign: BROKEN - the constructor never runs, so declare() never runs; children is the PARENT Map by prototype (own_children false), and adding one child took the parent from 2 to 3; url and name stay the parents and naming() cannot re-derive them because every field is truthy through the prototype. (c) config derivation: constructor runs, fresh Map, url/name/title right, parent spec untouched; one caveat - a shallow spread SHARES nested objects, so a change replaces a whole key.

DECISION: (c) deriving the CONFIG. Each design file exports a plain spec object and does new Page(design(spec, {...})); derive(parent, changes) merges one level deep so one change reads as one line. Alternatives kept: (a) a subclass per design wins when the difference is BEHAVIOUR (a band that draws differently, not a value that differs) - it is the only one with real method seams; (b) Object.create wins nothing here and is refuted by measurement, but would be right for a throwaway clone that is never routed to and never declares children.

ux/Tree gap (consumed, not edited): Tree.Row.prerender decides the tag as (!item.kids && node.href) ? a : div, so a BRANCH row can never be a real link - only leaves are. The shell subclasses Row and calls View.prototype.prerender directly to get past it. A one-word change in ux/Tree (this.node.href ? a : div) would delete that override.

Router.mark_links() stamps .active on the anchor you are on and .in-path on its ancestors after EVERY navigation, cold deep link and Back included - so a tree of real links needs no selection state at all. ux/Tree select() is overridden to a no-op so there is one highlight, not two that only agree after a click.

assign.now: measuring - nav stability, the resize gesture, the three invariants at four widths

log.msg: NAV STABILITY, 0px. Clicked all 7 designs in turn plus a 600px viewport scroll, re-reading the sidebar track x, its width and the first five rows y after every step: worst drift 0.00px at 1280, 1920 and 3440, across viewport content heights of 1000-1454px. Zero console errors. The mechanism: the shell is height:100% and neither region grows past it, so there is no page scroll to move the rail; position:sticky top:0 in the stretched track is the guarantee if a future design ever makes the shell scroll.

RESIZE, driven headless with real pointer events. 288px (18rem default) -> drag to 224 = 14rem exactly, readout 14rem, localStorage lew42:/layouts/shell/ = {px:224} -> reload keeps 224 -> drag to 640 = 40rem -> drag to 40px clamps to 192 = the 12rem floor -> drag to 1800px clamps to 960 = half of 1920 -> double-click resets to 288 and writes px:null. The floor and ceiling are CSS (clamp(12rem, var(--std-shell-rail), 50%)), never JS, so they stay right when the window is resized.

THREE INVARIANTS inside the viewport, at 400/1280/1920/3440 over 6 pages: no text or framed box at the viewport edge (0), no prose past the measure (0), no constant where a token exists. One deliberate scroller per page - the viewport - and no horizontal overflow anywhere. Two findings fixed on the way: a page-title and 48px of page padding above the first band (the design now starts at the viewport edge, /layouts/practice/ hides its title the same way), and a summary dressed as a button, 341px of bordered grey inside a 1632px band.

WALL COUNTS. An auto-fill wall of six cards sat on FIVE columns with a last row of ONE at 1920 - the same failure /layouts/practice/catalog/ measured at 2800-3360. Replaced with a written-out ladder 1/2/3/count: at 400/700/1000/1280/1600/1920/2560/3440 the rows are [1x6],[2,2,2],[2,2,2],[3,3],[3,3],[6],[6],[6] for the base and [3,3] everywhere above 46rem for the derived one - no short row at any width. Card widths 212-525px, all inside the measure. Also: a written-out count needs a CEILING - three equal columns of a 3152px viewport made a card sentence 829px (51em), and capping the wall alone left 1500px of dead ground between the wall and the rail beside it, so the cap is on the COLUMN.

assign.outcome:
**A sidebar that never moves, resizable to any width, and a viewport beside it holding a tree of eight homepage designs derived one change at a time** — [/layouts/shell/](/layouts/shell/). Drag the sidebar's right edge; click a row.

![the shell at 1920, sidebar at 14rem](/layouts/shell/shots/shell-1920-14rem.jpg)

[At 40rem](/layouts/shell/shots/shell-1920-40rem.jpg) · [the deepest design](/layouts/shell/home/taller-hero/no-wall/dark-band/) · [at 400, a top strip](/layouts/shell/shots/shell-400-strip.jpg) · [the doc](/layouts/shell/doc/pages/)

**The sidebar does not move: 0.00px.** Clicked all seven designs in turn plus a 600px viewport scroll, re-reading the track's x, its width and the first five rows' y after each — worst drift 0px at 1280, 1920 and 3440, across viewport content heights of 1000–1454px. The shell is `height: 100%` and both regions own their scrolling, so there is no page scroll to move the rail; `position: sticky` in the stretched track is the guarantee for the day one does.

**Resize:** 18rem default → 14rem → reload keeps it → 40rem → past the floor clamps to 12rem → past the ceiling clamps to half the room → double-click resets. The floor and ceiling are CSS, never JS, so they stay right when the window is resized. The width is the only thing that persists.

**Derivation — decided: derive the CONFIG.** A child imports its parent's plain spec object and changes one key; `new Page(…)` then runs the whole constructor, so `declare()` runs, `children` is a fresh Map and `meta: import.meta` gives the child its own url. *Alternative kept:* a subclass per design wins when the difference is behaviour rather than a value — it is the only one with real method seams. *Refuted by measurement:* `Object.create(parentPage)` never runs the constructor, so `children` is the parent's own Map — adding one child to the clone took the parent from two to three — and `naming()` can never re-derive the url. [The three, in full](/layouts/shell/doc/pages/).

**Eight designs, four levels deep, eight rows in the sidebar** — the two numbers agree because the rail walks the real pages. Twelve urls crawled at 400/1280/1920/3440: zero console errors, no text at a viewport edge, no prose past the measure, no horizontal overflow, one deliberate scroller per page.

**Fixed on the way:** the base design showed *both* itself and the routed one (core's columns rule leaves a `default` ANCESTOR showing; a two-region shell needs the contract's own later-marked-sibling test); an `auto-fill` wall of six sat on five columns with a last row of one at 1920; a written-out count with no ceiling made a card's sentence 829px at 3440 and left 1,500px of dead ground beside the rail; a `<summary>` rendered as 341px of bordered grey because framework.css dresses `summary` as a button; 48px of page padding above the first band.

**Left:** real pages moving on disk when dragged (no server in production — a later task) · pages in a database (the scouts' reports) · `ux/Tree` cannot make a BRANCH row a link — `Shell.js` subclasses past it, and one word there would delete the override (consumed, not edited, by fence).

log.msg: SKILL IMPROVEMENT, logged rather than written - .claude/skills/ is outside this brief fence, so the mastermind should apply it. layout/SKILL.md says "walls take grid auto-fill, only a control row takes flex wrap" two lines after it says wrapping layouts misalign at awkward counts. Those disagree, and the site has already measured which is right: /layouts/practice/catalog/ replaced an auto-fill wall that sat on five columns from 2800 to 3360, and this task hit the same shape at 1920 (six cards, five columns, a last row of one). Suggested line for layout/improvements.md: "A WALL WITH A KNOWN CARD COUNT WRITES ITS COLUMN COUNTS OUT - a ladder of divisors (1/2/3/6 for six cards) in container queries - and takes a per-column CEILING. auto-fill is for a wall whose count is unknown; with a known count it puts a short row somewhere at some width, and above ~34rem a column the card sentence passes the measure. Measured twice: catalog 2026-09-17, shell-lab 2026-09-17."

CORE NOTE for the docs pass, no edit made (fence): core Page css stands a default child down with "> .page.default:not(.active-page, .active-ancestor)", which is right for a COLUMNS host, where an ancestor column is still a column in the row, and wrong for any host whose region REPLACES one child with another - a default base page is also the parent of its siblings, so it stays marked as an ancestor and both paint. The two-region form is "> .page.default:has(~ .page:is(.active-page, .active-ancestor))", which is the same question the arrangement contract already asks of an ancestor. Worth a line in core/Page/doc/css.md beside the .default twins.
